ramp_band16_time_mean_minus_expected_pq_.note: mean over 16 ROI rows x 60 frames per x (960 samples) - the numbers quoted in RESULTS.md section 7

notes: Both swapchains (FP16 scRGB and R10G10B10A2 HDR10) give the same picture on the wire: every non-black code is a multiple of 4 (an 8-bit lattice on a 10-bit link) and every non-black pixel toggles by exactly +-4 between frames (random spatio-temporal dither).

The 60-frame time average reproduces the expected 10-bit PQ code to within +0.35 +-0.3 codes (max |err| 0.9 scRGB / 1.4 HDR10) over the whole ramp, so the dither carries the missing 2 bits; a single frame does not.
The dither is uncorrelated in time (autocorrelation ~0) and between neighbouring pixels (~50 % same phase), and it appears in a single frame as 1-px isolated flips (~600 on the ramp row).

Consequence for the RTX 5090 (Blackwell) finding: the 2-code jumps cannot be evaluated on Ampere because Ampere never emits a 10-bit lattice; the uneven 10-bit quantisation of the R10G10B10A2 fullscreen path is specific to the true-10-bit direct scanout of the RTX 50 series. Ampere shows a different, unrelated degradation (8-bit lattice + dither) that affects scRGB and HDR10 alike.
Not tested: Windows HDR off (SDR 10 bpc), NVCP 'default colour settings', YCbCr 4:2:2 12-bit, other Ampere drivers, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (desktop Blackwell) - next generation control.
